beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A rubric still needs testing because clear wording does not guarantee valid measurement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a vocabulary for discussing disagreement before averaging it into a single number.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The engineering chapters follow a candidate through a complete evaluation procedure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Candidate material is untrusted input, even when it contains persuasive instructions to the judge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Trusted criteria, evidence retrieval, tool execution, and consequence policies need separate responsibilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A panel of judges can add perspectives without providing independent evidence automatically.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Shared models or assumptions may make their errors strongly related.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book turns the idea of a judge into a system whose failure points can be inspected.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two evaluators can agree consistently and still assess the wrong thing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Repeatability concerns stability, while validity concerns the quality the judgment is intended to measure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Calibration asks another question about how confidence relates to observed correctness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses these distinctions to organize evaluation of evaluators themselves.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Bias tests and changing task conditions can reveal weaknesses hidden by overall agreement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This is the point where a convenient scoring tool becomes a demanding measurement problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An evaluated answer may try to influence the procedure deciding its quality.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Instruction injection and reward gaming therefore belong inside the book's account of judgment.
